title: Interpretation of Legislation Act 1984
why: The Victorian rules of statutory interpretation: how Acts and subordinate instruments are construed (Part II and Part III), commencement, repeal and amendment effects, definitions of common terms (s 38), time (s 44), the construction of "may" and "shall" (s 45), service by post (s 49), authorised versions (Part V) and regulations (s 65).

text.converter: vic_convert3.py (stdlib zipfile + ElementTree over word/document.xml and word/endnotes.xml; kept outside the repository). It fails on any paragraph style, run element or symbol character it was not written for.
text.conversion: The Word file was converted to UTF-8 plain text by Legalese Commons (vic_convert3.py: stdlib zipfile and ElementTree over word/document.xml and word/endnotes.xml). The table of provisions, running heads and footers are dropped; the cover is kept as the file prints it (twice). Each provision starts on its own line with its number; paragraphs are indented two spaces a level; the register's marginal history notes are kept as "[Side note: ...]" lines before the provision they annotate; tables are "| a | b |" rows; no-break spaces become plain spaces and no-break hyphens become hyphens. The Word file holds no equation, drawing, picture or embedded object, so there is no formulas sidecar, and it holds no Symbol-font character (the only symbol characters are the rule above Endnotes). Bold and italic (defined terms, Act titles) are not carried. The four Word endnotes (the quoted text of amending provisions, printed under "3 Explanatory details") are kept at the end, each under an "[Endnote N]" line, and "[endnote N]" marks the four places in the text where the Word file refers to one. The Act's own Endnotes section (general information, table of amendments, explanatory details) is kept. Apart from the marks and labels listed above, no non-space character is added, dropped or changed (checked by counting every character of the Word file's text against the converted text); line breaks and tabs inside a paragraph become spaces, paragraph ends are trimmed and empty paragraphs are dropped.
known_conversion_artefacts: the cover (version number, title, number, version date) appears twice at the head, as in the Word file
the "Note" label stands on its own line, unindented, before its text

the four Word-endnote texts are carried under "3 Explanatory details" in the order the Word file refers to them, each under an "[Endnote N]" line that the Word file does not have; only Endnote 3 holds side notes

in Endnote 3 (the quoted text of s 43 of the Supreme Court Act 1986) the line "the time is standard time as provided in subsection (1) ..." is set by the register in a numbered-paragraph style with no number; it is carried as an indented run-on line
the register's side notes read "Commis-sioner", "Common-wealth" and "communi-cation" with a literal hyphen in the Word file; they are carried as printed
cells of the Table of Amendments are carried one cell per column, so a row reads "| Assent Date: | 3.12.85 |"

check_against_authorised_pdf_2026_11_11.method: The authorised PDF was converted with pdftotext -bbox-layout; running heads, footers and the front matter (cover and table of provisions, PDF pages 1-4) were removed; margin notes were separated from the body by position; a line-end hyphen was joined to the next line on the PDF side; whitespace was normalised on both sides; nothing else.

parts_and_schedules.note: 6 Parts and Schedule 1; the Endnotes heading is the 8th entry in the Word table

differences_all_accounted_for: the PDF cover reads "Authorised Version No. 134" and "Authorised Version incorporating amendments as at" where the Word cover reads "Version No. 134" and "Version incorporating amendments as at" (2 places)
the PDF breaks the line after the em dash in s 19(1)(aa)(i) ("number— as" against "number—as")

the PDF prints the four Word-endnote reference numbers in the text (s 32 heading, the s 38 definition of Court of Appeal, s 44(5), s 57 heading) and the numbers 1 to 4 before each endnote; the converted text marks them "[endnote N]" and "[Endnote N]"
the two side notes quoted inside Endnote 3 are body text on the PDF side and side notes on the Word side
in the PDF reading order the cell labels of the Table of Amendments entry for the Sheriff Act 2009 come apart from their values; the words are the same
